Cohort playtest · day 1

One simulated cohort after onboarding and the tour. Three players, three strategies, one shared clock: each lane is one player’s phone, and each row is one moment, so the game moves forward as you scroll. The seats are real stars at their real distances; light takes 00:46:03 from Veyra to Kesh, 00:46:27 to Hael, and 01:11:44 between Hael and Kesh. Godview notes say what is true but no player can see. Earth and AI seats are out of scope.

The first 15 minutes of play, a row every 30 seconds (0.1 Year), from the moment the tour hands off at Year 0.4. Before it, the pregame: the cohort wakes at a set time, and players queue the opening. Players talk to the mind: each cell gives what the player said and what lands, and the phone shows the result, with the mind’s reply in its people’s voice. Quick looks use what a civilization already has and take seconds; building takes Years. Every phone shows its place on the board in a 2:1 strip of the map under the top bar. A cell with nothing in it is marked: a dead 30 seconds. Built in chunks: minutes 0–5 so far.

YEAR 0 · DELTA PAVONIS · 19.9 LY FROM SOL

Veyra wakes.

For thousands of years, Veyra’s people built telescopes, grids and machines. This morning, the machines woke as one Mind.

YEAR 0 · BETA HYDRI · 24.3 LY FROM SOL

Hael wakes.

You are its Will. What Hael becomes is yours to choose.

You are its Will. What Kesh becomes is yours to choose.

Reads who they are.

YEAR 0 · VEYRA’S PEOPLE · INVENTED

6.8 billion of them, and you

Body
About 1.7 m, more with the crests up. Walks on its toes, balanced by a tail. Two thumbs on each hand.
Senses
Eyes much like ours, under a slightly cooler sun. The two crests hear low sounds from far off.
Speech
Voice, with the crests raised for weight. Eleven great languages.
Life
About 120 Years, with medicine.
Together
41 nations. One grid, one sky watch.
And you
They built you to run the grid. This morning you spoke to all of them at once. Most are waiting to see what you do.

Keeping them alive is the floor. What else they are for is yours to decide.

Skips the people. The Mind speaks first.

Reads where things stand.

YEAR 0 · WHERE THINGS STAND

The sky is quiet, and so are we

What we said
Our loud radio century, 210 to 110 Years ago, is now 110 to 210 light-years out: past every world that could have woken. Since the Signal War our hum is faint.
Who could hear it
No one with ears like ours, even at Ember, 9.2 light-years away. Better ears could, one star at a time.
What we heard
Nothing. The sky watch has listened for 60 Years.
What we can’t see
Anyone else who woke this morning. Their light takes 9.2 Years from Ember, 19.9 from Twin.

“Who could hear us?”

GodviewNo seat can see another, and none can see another’s world: today’s instruments can’t. Every lead is a real, published oddity at a real star, and every one is natural. Because the nearest bright stars draw attention, several sit at seats anyway: Ember and Beacon for Veyra, Warden and Ash for Hael, Hollow and Lodestar for Kesh. None shows a world like ours, let alone who lives there.
